In [[demographics]], the '''rank mobility index (RMI)''' is a measure of a [[city]]'s change in population rank among a group of cities.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=D'Agostino |first=Marcello |last2=Dardanoni |first2=Valentino |date=2009-07-01 |title=The measurement of rank mobility |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022053108001609 |journal=Journal of Economic Theory |volume=144 |issue=4 |pages=1783–1803 |doi=10.1016/j.jet.2008.11.003 |issn=0022-0531|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Sheng |first=Kerong |last2=Fan |first2=Jie |last3=Sun |first3=Wei |last4=Ma |first4=Hailong |date=2016-06-01 |title=From sequential to parallel growth of cities: Theory and evidence from Canada |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s11769-015-0750-5 |journal=Chinese Geographical Science |language=en |volume=26 |issue=3 |pages=377–388 |doi=10.1007/s11769-015-0750-5 |issn=1993-064X|doi-access=free }}</ref>

Formally

:<math>RMI=\frac{R_1-R_2}{R_1+R_2},</math>

where

* ''R''<sub>1</sub> = city's rank at time 1
* ''R''<sub>2</sub> = city's rank at time 2

A RMI value must be between &minus;1 and 1. A RMI of 0 indicates no change.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Greene |first=Richard P. |url=https://www.google.pt/books/edition/Exploring_the_Urban_Community/qJxNAQAAIAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&bsq=rank+mobility+index+(RMI)&dq=rank+mobility+index+(RMI)&printsec=frontcover |title=Exploring the Urban Community: A GIS Approach |last2=Pick |first2=James B. |date=2006 |publisher=Pearson Prentice Hall |isbn=978-0-13-017576-2 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Greene |first=Richard P. |last2=Pick |first2=James B. |date=2013-06-01 |title=Shifting patterns of suburban dominance: the case of Chicago from 2000 to 2010 |url=https://doi.org/10.1080/17445647.2013.782257 |journal=Journal of Maps |volume=9 |issue=2 |pages=178–182 |doi=10.1080/17445647.2013.782257}}</ref>
